name: vwap_cross_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When price crosses above VWAP on elevated volume after being below for 20+ bars, it signals a regime shift: the marginal buyer is now paying above the session's volume-weighted fair value. Institutional VWAP-tracking algorithms that were selling now become buyers, creating a positive feedback loop. The edge exists because the cross event is a Schelling point — many participants watch VWAP, and their collective response to the cross creates a brief momentum burst that outruns transaction costs. The edge is not arbitraged because it requires very fast reaction (<1 min) and the absolute profit per trade is small.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 30 crore INR AND beta(NIFTY50, 60) between 0.8 and 1.5

long.confirmation: cross bar closes in top 30% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) > 0.7

short.confirmation: cross bar closes in bottom 30% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) < 0.3

entry.entry_price: market order at confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: VWAP (re-cross back below/above VWAP) OR 0.25% from entry, whichever is hit first
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-crosses VWAP in opposite direction

filters.vix_filter: no filter — momentum works in all VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:45 (let VWAP stabilize) or after 14:45
filters.volume_filter: volume surge > 2x 10-bar SMA on cross bar
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when NIFTY 50 is green for the day, shorts when red
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry day (whipsaws increase)
other_filters: skip if stock has crossed VWAP > 5 times already today (choppy)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — VWAP cross is widely watched; edge depends on speed of entry

weaknesses: In range-bound days, VWAP gets crossed many times — strategy generates false signals and accumulates losses
The 20-bar requirement means missing the first (most powerful) VWAP cross of the day
Volume surge threshold of 2x may be too aggressive, filtering out valid signals in low-vol stocks
prior_art: VWAP crossover is a staple of retail day trading (Bellafiore, 'One Good Trade'). Academic work by Berkowitz et al. (1988) established VWAP as a benchmark. The cross-with-dwell-time filter (20 bars below) is less common and adds originality.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 40bps - 0.52 * 25bps = 19.2 - 13.0 = 6.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps RT. Gross edge insufficient. Need to either tighten stops to 0.20% or increase target to 0.5% to improve the math. The 20-bar dwell filter should improve win rate above 0.48 — backtest validation needed.
